title: Parallel harness execution
intent: Let several harnesses attack distinct Works at the same time — one harness per Work — with filesystem and shared-state isolation strong enough that no run can impact another
motivation: The demand splits at the isolation boundary: where a run executes (its own worktree, never the shared checkout) is a different mechanism and a different verification from whether shared Git state (manifest refs, locks, the worktree registry) survives overlapping runs. Mixing them would make a failure unreadable.
ordering: Isolation first, because the concurrency proof must exercise the final execution shape; proving safety and then changing where runs execute would prove nothing.
